name: NJ-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Hamawy's large fundraising and outside support advantage
Republican nominee underfunded with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean and an open-seat Democratic nominee who has raised over $1.5 million with nearly $2 million in outside support against a Republican with under $80,000 raised make this safely Democratic. Markets price a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually strong GOP candidate campaign could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Bonnie Watson Coleman's retirement leaves this central New Jersey seat open, but the district's D+13 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic column territory. Adam Hamawy enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.5 million and benefited from nearly $2 million in outside support, while Republican Gregg Mele has raised under $80,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars on hand.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the spending gap. Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 97%. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but lack visible resources. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the winning margin rather than the outcome.
